slot.brief: Straightforward indefinite/definite integral reducible by a single substitution (t = inner function); easy 2/5 with clean derivative present.

verdicts.working: An antiderivative is \(\ln(1+x^2)\). Evaluating from 0 to 1 gives \(\ln 2\).

working:
Let $t=1+x^2$, so $dt=2x\,dx$. Then $\displaystyle\int_0^1 \dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\,dx=\int_1^2 \dfrac{dt}{t}=\ln 2$.

Independent check: An antiderivative is \(\ln(1+x^2)\). Evaluating from 0 to 1 gives \(\ln 2\).

draft.distractor_notes: A: introduces an extra factor of $\dfrac{1}{2}$. C: introduces an extra factor of $2$. D: treats the integrand as having antiderivative $1+x^2$.
